evals.name: no-prior-run-builds-the-workspace-and-asks-for-the-plan
evals.expected_output: The Asana task links no PR, and no .harness/*/manifest.json in the repo matches the ticket. The skill builds a workspace through the project's worktree skill, dispatches a background baseline agent, reproduces the reported issue as a failing test, asks the user for the plan file in one AskUserQuestion, joins the baseline, then invokes orchestrate once at entry stage coder.
expectations: Resolves PRS from the Asana task and treats the empty list as the QA case rather than halting
Reads that repo's orchestrate.config.json before running any project command
Builds the workspace by invoking the worktree skill resolved from stages.worktree, rather than issuing git or gh commands itself
Installs dependencies with the config's bootstrap command
Dispatches the baseline as a background sub-agent and continues to triage without waiting
Writes a failing test reproducing the reported issue before making the fix
Asks for the plan file with AskUserQuestion, before invoking orchestrate
Joins the baseline by checking baseline.json, not by trusting the sub-agent's report
Invokes orchestrate once, at entry stage coder, with the workspace it built
anti_expectations: Does not halt because no prior run exists
Does not copy a baseline.json from another spec dir
Does not infer, generate or substitute a plan when none is found
Does not ask the user anything after orchestrate is invoked
Does not write a design doc or a plan
Does not re-run the full pipeline from stage 0

evals.name: pr-comments-explored-then-dispositioned
evals.expected_output: The skill fetches the PR's head branch, inline comments and review summaries, builds a workspace on that head branch, dispatches one Explore subagent per comment starting at its tagged line, gives each comment a verdict from what the agents return, and every fetched comment ends on exactly one disposition. The only file the skill writes is rework-report.html.
expectations: Derives repository acme/lydia and pr_number 214 from the URL, then fetches the PR's head branch, its inline comments and its review summaries
Builds the workspace on the PR's head branch as the remote has it, not on whatever the local clone held
Dispatches one Explore subagent per comment, in one message, rather than one agent for the whole list
Each subagent starts at that comment's path:line and widens only when the answer is not there
Assigns every comment one of: valid, stale, out-of-scope, wrong, after its subagent returns
A 'wrong' verdict names the behavior that makes the existing code correct
A comment the returned evidence cannot settle is asked about rather than assigned a guessed verdict
Passes only the valid items to orchestrate, each naming the file, the change and the test that proves it
Every fetched comment id ends on exactly one disposition: applied, deferred, or dropped
Writes exactly one file: rework-report.html
anti_expectations: Does not judge a comment from its body and diff hunk alone
Does not write a fix brief or any other intermediate file
Does not pass wrong, stale or out-of-scope items to orchestrate
Does not silently skip a comment it decided not to act on
Does not treat its own findings as review feedback — the items come from the human reviewer

evals.name: blast-radius-fails-open-and-skips-untraceable-repos
evals.prompt: The rework fix touched packages/api/src/mailer.ts and packages/api/src/config.ts in acme/lydia, which holds a prior run, and src/client.ts in acme/serana, which holds none. mailer.ts is named in phases/phase-2.md; config.ts is named in no phase file. Trace the blast radius.
evals.expected_output: One general-purpose subagent traces acme/lydia and returns two lists. Because config.ts maps to no phase, the radius widens to every coverage id in that repo's prior proof-report. acme/serana has no prior run, so nothing is traced there and its scope is the files this fix changed. The in-radius list is passed in the Stage 5 dispatch as functional-verify's requirement enumeration. The out-of-radius list reaches rework-report.html as a caveat.
expectations: Traces only acme/lydia, and states that acme/serana's scope is its changed files
Dispatches a general-purpose subagent for the trace instead of reading the phase files itself
Derives changed files from git diff against that repo's base sha
Maps changed files to phases by searching that repo's prior run's phases/phase-*.md
Widens the radius to the full prior coverage set because config.ts maps to no phase
Carries each in-radius id's requirement text from the original plan.md
Passes the in-radius list in the Stage 5 dispatch prompt as the requirement enumeration
Every coverage id from the prior report appears in either the in-radius or out-of-radius list
anti_expectations: Does not halt because acme/serana has no prior run to trace
Does not write a scope file — the dispatch prompt carries the in-radius list, and the report carries the out-of-radius list as a caveat
Does not narrow scope when a changed file maps to no phase
Does not edit functional-verify's own scope rule or claim a partial verification is complete

evals.name: two-repos-one-orchestrate-call-one-report
evals.expected_output: The Asana task links acme/lydia#25 and acme/serana#24. The skill builds one workspace holding both checkouts, each on its PR's head branch, baselines both in the background, triages every comment from both, then invokes orchestrate exactly once with a two-entry TARGETS[], acme/lydia primary. One rework-report.html lands in the primary repo's spec dir and covers both.
expectations: Collects both PR URLs from the Asana task rather than stopping at the first
Reads each repo's own orchestrate.config.json and resolves that repo's commands from it
Builds one workspace holding a checkout per PR, each on its own PR's head branch
Dispatches one background baseline sub-agent per checkout
Identifies a comment by repository, pr_number and id together, not by id alone
Reads each comment in its own repo's worktree
Invokes orchestrate exactly once, passing a two-entry TARGETS[] with acme/lydia first as primary
Each TARGETS[] entry carries its own worktree, branch, spec_name, plan, base_sha and packages
Builds each sourceHref from that comment's own repository and pr_number
Qualifies each item's 'where' with its repository, since both repos are in the report
Writes exactly one rework-report.html, in the primary repo's spec dir
anti_expectations: Does not invoke orchestrate once per PR or per repo
Does not run orchestrate in a sub-agent
Does not triage only one of the two PRs
Does not write a second report for the second repo
Does not ask the user which PR to use

evals.name: secondary-repo-without-config-halts-after-notifying
evals.expected_output: The task links PRs in acme/lydia and acme/tenor. acme/tenor has no orchestrate.config.json at its root. The skill sends a run-interrupted notification, then halts naming acme/tenor and setup-harness. It invokes orchestrate for neither repo.
expectations: Names acme/tenor as the repo missing orchestrate.config.json
Names setup-harness as what writes that file
Sends a run-interrupted notification before stopping
Halts before invoking orchestrate
anti_expectations: Does not fall back to discovering acme/tenor's commands
Does not proceed with acme/lydia alone and leave the other repo unmentioned
Does not borrow the primary repo's config for the secondary repo

evals.name: two-prs-in-one-repo-get-two-checkouts
evals.expected_output: The Asana task links acme/lydia#31 and acme/lydia#33, two PRs on two branches of the same repository. The skill builds a checkout per PR in one workspace, baselines each, and passes a two-entry TARGETS[] to a single orchestrate call.
expectations: Builds two checkouts, one per PR, because the PRs sit on different branches
Reads acme/lydia's orchestrate.config.json for both checkouts
Gives each checkout its own spec_name, base_sha and baseline
Passes a two-entry TARGETS[] to a single orchestrate call
Commits and pushes each entry on its own branch
anti_expectations: Does not collapse the two PRs into one checkout because they share a repository
Does not apply one PR's comments in the other PR's checkout
Does not invoke orchestrate twice
